gaps.sentence: By the time the fire crew arrived, the neighbours ___ the blaze out with buckets of water.
gaps.explanation: The putting out happened before the crew arrived: past perfect 'had put'.

gaps.sentence: The train ___ faster than the bus, so we always take the train.
gaps.explanation: Timeless comparisons take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: I ___ the dentist on Thursday afternoon — I booked it last week.
gaps.explanation: A personal arrangement already made takes the present continuous: am seeing.

gaps.sentence: The neighbours ___ the flames with buckets for an hour by the time the firemen arrived.
gaps.explanation: 'For an hour by the time … arrived' — past perfect continuous for duration before a past moment.

gaps.sentence: Don't wake him — he has just ___ asleep.
gaps.explanation: 'Has just' is followed by the past participle: fallen.

gaps.sentence: Her eyes were red because she ___.
gaps.hint: visible result of an earlier activity
gaps.explanation: The past perfect continuous shows an activity whose results were visible at a past moment: had been crying.

gaps.sentence: She ___ three novels since she retired.
gaps.explanation: 'Since she retired' (up to now) — present perfect.

gaps.sentence: This month they ___ a new wing to the hospital, so some services are elsewhere.
gaps.hint: this month means a temporary current period
gaps.explanation: 'This month' describes a temporary situation around now, so the present continuous fits: are adding.
